bull_argument.argument:
IOI Properties' CFO rose from RM1.060bn to RM2.391bn, and cash after specified property/land/PP&E outlays but before acquisitions and interest was RM1.780bn. That operating improvement creates a plausible purchase scenario in which the expanded asset base supplies recurring rent, collections and earnings. Growing revenue provides a foundation beyond the annual profit-doubling headline.

Net debt of RM21.818bn before leases and borrowings growth of about 29.4% make this speculative. Fair-value and JV remeasurement gains contributed 51.31% of PBT, so 8.54x trailing earnings cannot establish cheapness; estimated forward P/E is 17.71x. Acquisitions and deposits exceeded the operating investment surplus and required net drawdowns. Better CFO makes successful conversion conceivable, not self-funding proven. The downtrend supplies no timing confirmation; buying requires recurring asset returns to catch up with financing commitments.
key_points: Improved CFO and pre-acquisition investment surplus anchor the operating scenario.
Noncash gains invalidate a simple low-trailing-P/E bargain claim.
Heavy net debt and acquisition funding make returns conditional on asset conversion.

bear_argument.argument:
IOI Properties' CFO improvement is real, but fair-value and JV remeasurement gains account for 51.31% of PBT. The 8.54x trailing multiple therefore gives a distorted impression of cheap recurring earnings; estimated forward P/E of 17.71x is materially less forgiving. Borrowings rose about 29.4%, producing RM21.818bn net debt before leases.

The bull's RM1.780bn investment surplus excludes acquisitions and interest. RM3.340bn investing outflow and RM3.258bn net borrowing drawdowns demonstrate financing dependence rather than merely unknown future returns. Expanded assets can earn recurring income, but current collection improvements have not funded that expansion. The downtrend adds timing caution without proving insolvency. Quantified leverage and noncash earnings make the prospective asset-return scenario insufficient protection at the headline valuation.
key_points: Noncash gains contribute over half of PBT.
Acquisition expansion depended on borrowing drawdowns.
Pre-acquisition cash surplus is not distributable owner cash.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's improved operating surplus is credible but excludes the acquisitions and interest that matter to enlarged net debt. RM3.258bn borrowing drawdowns show that successful future conversion is being financed before its returns are delivered.

bull_argument.argument:
The bear correctly rejects headline P/E as clean recurring value when fair-value and remeasurement gains contribute 51.31% of PBT. The narrower counterweight is that CFO rose to RM2.391bn from RM1.060bn and retained RM1.780bn after the specified property, equipment and land spending. Operating cash improvement therefore exists independently of treating noncash gains as owner earnings.

Acquisition and deposit spending still required net borrowing, and RM21.818bn net debt leaves a substantial financing burden. The higher-risk purchase scenario is completed acquisitions and property operations improving recurring cash enough to reduce that dependence; no verified recurring valuation proves this is priced in. Actual cash-generating operations keep that scenario plausible, while forward P/E of 17.71x is more relevant than 8.54x headline earnings. Buying remains speculative until asset conversion and funding discipline substantiate shareholder participation.
key_points: Noncash gains invalidate a simple headline-P/E bargain.
Operating cash improved after specified ordinary asset spending.
Acquisition returns must reduce observed borrowing dependence.
bull_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: Funding dependence is real. However, RM1.780bn remains from operating CFO after the specified ordinary asset spending before acquisitions and interest; the operating engine is not solely noncash profit. This supports a speculative conversion thesis without declaring debt manageable or valuation already cheap.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull's RM2.391bn CFO and RM1.780bn surplus after specified property, equipment and land spend confirm operating improvement independently of noncash gains. This answers any claim that the asset base produces no cash. It does not resolve the difference between that surplus and expansion financed through RM3.258bn net borrowing drawdowns.

Borrowings rose roughly 29.4%, with RM21.818bn net debt before leases. Fair-value and JV remeasurement account for 51.31% of PBT, so 8.54x trailing earnings misstates recurring cheapness; 17.71x forecast earnings is less forgiving. Acquisitions can improve future recurring income, but current leverage and funding requirements are already large rather than merely unknown. The bull preserves a speculative asset-return scenario. Against it, the combination of distorted earnings and financing dependence supplies concrete downside exposure that improved operating CFO has not yet outweighed.
key_points: Operating CFO improvement is independently real.
Expansion required substantial borrowing beyond the investment surplus.
Recurring valuation is less forgiving than headline trailing P/E.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers cash existence but not the debt-funded expansion burden or recurring price compensation. Its speculative scenario remains plausible, while quantified financing dependence keeps the current risk/reward weak.

bull_case_summary: IOI Properties has CFO rising to RM2.391bn and RM1.780bn after specified ordinary asset outlays before acquisitions and interest. Round two uses this real operating contribution to preserve a speculative asset-conversion scenario independent of noncash gains.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts operating cash but notes RM3.258bn net borrowing drawdowns and RM21.818bn net debt before leases. Noncash gains comprise 51.31% of PBT, so the 8.54x headline multiple overstates recurring cheapness versus 17.71x forecasts.
key_points_of_agreement: Noncash gains make headline reported valuation misleading.
The ordinary investment surplus excludes acquisitions and interest.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether future asset conversion can compensate already-observed financing dependence and less-forgiving recurring valuation.
unresolved_uncertainties: Delivered recurring returns from acquisitions and property operations.
Funding discipline and sustained cash after all expansion and interest demands.
